info.title: ClipMux integration API
info.description: The routes an app's backend, its browser uploader and its player use, and the webhooks the app receives. Requests and responses are JSON, with bodies up to 64 KiB. Every POST takes an `Idempotency-Key`. Errors are `{"error": {"code", "message", ...details}}`; a `429 rate_limited` carries `Retry-After`. The management API, which the dashboard uses with the owner's session, is not described here.

post.description: Call from your backend, then hand the body to the browser uploader. The asset exists at once in `waiting_upload`, with its playback IDs, so you can store them before the file arrives. `generate` asks for subtitles and chapters once the video is ready; `renditions` limits the ladder.

200.description: Signed URLs; PUT each part and keep its ETag

post.description: Up to 100 part numbers at a time. PUT each part's bytes to its URL before `expires_at`, and keep the `ETag` storage returns for each.

get.description: The parts storage already holds, so an upload can resume after a dropped connection or a closed tab.

post.description: Send every part's number and `ETag`. The asset moves to `processing`, and encoding starts.
Stops the upload. The asset becomes `errored` with `error_code` `upload_cancelled`. Takes the upload token or an API key with `uploads:write`.

post.summary: Import from a URL, or attach a PC agent's local file
post.description: Two ways to make an asset without an upload. With `url`, the server fetches a public http(s) URL and encodes it; a non-public or credentialed URL is `400 import_url_refused`, and a fetch that fails ends `errored` with `import_url_refused`, `import_failed` or `import_too_large`. With `agent_source_id`, it attaches a file a PC agent registered for `clipmux push --local`, and its jobs run only on that agent.

get.summary: Find by passthrough, or page through changes

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Every change since this time, oldest first, deleted included.

get.description: With `passthrough`, the app's assets with that reference, newest first. With `updated_since`, every change since an RFC 3339 time, oldest first, deleted assets included, up to 100 a page with `next_cursor`: the way to catch up after missed webhooks.
The asset, as it is now. Keep the highest `version` you have seen.

patch.description: Sets the title; `""` or `null` clears it. A change raises `version` and sends `video.asset.updated`; the same title changes nothing.

delete.description: Playback stops at once. `200` once the files are gone, `202` while the delete job runs.

post.description: Encodes the source again, for example with other `renditions`. The current output keeps playing until the new one is ready. `409 job_active` (with `job_id`) while another job changes the asset; `supersede` cancels it.

409.description: asset_not_ready, no_audio, subtitles_not_ready, chapters_not_connected, job_active, asset_deleted, idempotency_in_progress

post.description: Makes a new subtitles or chapters track. The old one keeps playing until the new one is ready. Chapters need ready subtitles and a connected LLM.

200.description: The track; chapters once a chapters track is ready

get.description: A track, with its chapters once a chapters track is ready.

delete.description: Removes a track: its file and transcript go at once. `200` once no playlist lists it, `202` while it is unpublished.

example.text: Today we look at three ways to sort a list.

segments.text: Today we look at three ways to sort a list.

get.description: A subtitles track's transcript, from the moment the track reads `ready`; `409 track_not_ready` before. Add `words=true` for word timings.

post.description: Adds a playback ID. A `signed` one plays only with a token your backend signs; a `public` one plays for anyone with the URL.

delete.description: Revokes a playback ID: `200 revoked` once it is unpublished, `202 revoking` before. Its playback stops; the asset's other IDs keep playing.

post.description: Makes a share link and its own signed playback ID. `url` is the page to send. `name` is one line of up to 100 characters; `expires_at` must be in the future and can't be changed later. Allowed while the asset is processing.

get.description: The asset's share links, newest first, each with `views_30d`: its views over the last 30 UTC days.

delete.description: Revokes the link's playback ID: `200` once unpublished, `202` while revoking. Revoking again changes nothing.

post.summary: A signed master.m3u8 URL for a share link
post.description: A signed `master.m3u8` URL for players that can't open the share page. It can't refresh: it lasts until the link's expiry or the longest token lifetime, whichever is first, and stops when the link is revoked.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The created_at (RFC 3339) of the newest event you have; the poll waits for a newer one.

get.description: The app's webhook events created at or after `since` (default now), oldest first, up to 100. `body` is exactly what an endpoint receives. Long-polls up to `wait` seconds (at most 25) until an event is newer than `after`, the `created_at` of the newest event you have.

The key's own app. `base_url` is the media origin playback URLs start with; `upload_origins` are where a browser sends parts. With `base_url`, they are what a page's Content-Security-Policy must allow. A token's `exp - iat` may not exceed `max_token_lifetime_seconds`; `signing_keys` are the keys that still verify tokens, newest first.

Totals, the same number of whole buckets just before (`previous`), a zero-filled series (hourly for `24h`, daily otherwise; the last bucket is partial), storage bytes currently held (`storage`), and the top 10 live videos by views (`top_assets`). `unique_viewers` counts distinct `vid` claims in tokens (by hour for `24h`, by UTC day otherwise, excluding poster fetches) and is `null` when no view carried one.
The same for one video, without `top_assets`. A deleted video keeps its history.

post.description: Starts a pairing: show the `code` and open `verify_url`, where the owner checks the code and approves. The code works for 10 minutes. `429 too_many_pairings` while 10 wait for the owner.

200.description: The first poll after approval carries credentials, once

post.description: Poll every `interval_seconds`. The first poll after approval carries `credentials`, and is the only one that ever does: they are deleted as they are returned, so a later poll is `404 pairing_not_found`.

200.description: A token for the link's playback ID

post.description: What the share page's script asks for: a `v` token for the link's playback ID, valid until the earliest of the link's expiry, max(2 x duration, 4 h) and the longest token lifetime. A `viewer_id` of 16 to 64 `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` characters counts as a unique viewer.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: ES256 JWT signed with the app's key: header kid; claims sub (playback ID), aud (v, or t for posters only), iat, exp, optional vid.

get.description: 401 token_expired: fetch a new token. 403 denied: stop.
Only for a public playback ID.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: ES256 JWT signed with the app's key: header kid; claims sub (playback ID), aud (v, or t for posters only), iat, exp, optional vid.

get.description: A public playback ID's poster, a JPEG of a frame near the start.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: ES256 JWT signed with the app's key: header kid; claims sub (playback ID), aud (v, or t for posters only), iat, exp, optional vid.

get.description: A ready track's WebVTT file, for players that show subtitles from a sidecar file rather than the playlist. A chapters track's file is at the same path.

text/vtt.example:
WEBVTT

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:04.200
Today we look at three ways to sort a list.

get.description: A public playback ID's track as WebVTT.

text/vtt.example:

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:04.200

post.description: The video is ready to play: its first encode is done and published. Delivery is at least once and unordered: verify `X-Webhook-Signature` over the raw body, reject a timestamp more than 300 s off, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`, and re-fetch the asset before acting on it. Retries back off for 24 hours.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx; redirects are not followed.

post.description: The asset changed after it was ready: a re-encode finished, its title changed, a playback ID was published, or it moved storage. Re-fetch and keep the highest `version`. Delivery is at least once and unordered: verify `X-Webhook-Signature` over the raw body, reject a timestamp more than 300 s off, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`, and re-fetch the asset before acting on it. Retries back off for 24 hours.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx; redirects are not followed.

post.description: The video can't be played: the upload, import or first encode failed. `data.error_code` says why. Delivery is at least once and unordered: verify `X-Webhook-Signature` over the raw body, reject a timestamp more than 300 s off, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`, and re-fetch the asset before acting on it. Retries back off for 24 hours.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx; redirects are not followed.

post.description: A re-encode failed. The video keeps playing its previous output; `job.error_code` says why. Delivery is at least once and unordered: verify `X-Webhook-Signature` over the raw body, reject a timestamp more than 300 s off, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`, and re-fetch the asset before acting on it. Retries back off for 24 hours.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx; redirects are not followed.

post.description: The video was deleted, and its playback has stopped. Delivery is at least once and unordered: verify `X-Webhook-Signature` over the raw body, reject a timestamp more than 300 s off, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`, and re-fetch the asset before acting on it. Retries back off for 24 hours.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx; redirects are not followed.

post.description: A subtitles or chapters track is ready. `track` names it. Delivery is at least once and unordered: verify `X-Webhook-Signature` over the raw body, reject a timestamp more than 300 s off, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`, and re-fetch the asset before acting on it. Retries back off for 24 hours.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx; redirects are not followed.

post.description: A track couldn't be made. `track.error_code` says why, for example `no_audio`. Delivery is at least once and unordered: verify `X-Webhook-Signature` over the raw body, reject a timestamp more than 300 s off, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`, and re-fetch the asset before acting on it. Retries back off for 24 hours.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx; redirects are not followed.

post.description: A track was deleted. Delivery is at least once and unordered: verify `X-Webhook-Signature` over the raw body, reject a timestamp more than 300 s off, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`, and re-fetch the asset before acting on it. Retries back off for 24 hours.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx; redirects are not followed.

Error.description: Every error. Details sit beside code and message, all strings (e.g. retry_after, job_id).

id.description: The playback ID (pid_...) that goes in playback URLs.

policy.description: signed plays only with a token your backend signs; public plays for anyone with the URL.

playable.description: Whether the ID plays now: false until the asset has an output, and once revoked.

status.description: active, revoking while its routes are unpublished, then revoked.

share.description: Present when a share link owns this ID.

source.description: generated: made by speech recognition or an LLM.

language.description: The detected language code for subtitles, for example en or hi.

error_code.description: Why the track errored, for example no_audio or llm_not_connected.

app_id.description: The app the asset belongs to.

status.description: waiting_upload until the file arrives, processing while it encodes, then ready or errored; deleted once deleted.

version.description: Rises on every change; keep the highest seen.

passthrough.description: Your own reference, such as lesson_42. Absent when unset.

title.description: For people: not unique and never part of a URL. One line, up to 200 characters. Absent when unset.

renditions.description: The renditions this asset's outputs are encoded at; absent means every rung up to the source.

error_code.description: Why the asset is errored, for example upload_cancelled, import_failed or unsupported_source.

base_url.description: The media origin playback URLs start with.

playback_ids.description: Every playback ID, including revoked ones and those a share link owns.

duration_seconds.description: Null until the first output exists.

tracks.description: Subtitles and chapters tracks; retired and deleted tracks are not listed.

AssetSettings.description: What the new asset gets, the same for an upload, an import from a URL and a PC agent's file.

passthrough.description: Your own reference, up to 255 bytes; it comes back on the asset and its webhooks.

generate.description: Ask for subtitles and chapters once the video is ready; chapters imply subtitles.

PlaybackPolicies.description: One playback ID is made for each policy. Default ["signed"]; ["signed", "public"] makes both.

part_size.description: Bytes in every part but the last.

upload_token.description: Hand this to the browser; it reaches only this upload.

playback_ids.description: The asset's playback IDs, already made.

url.description: A public http or https URL; the server fetches it.

agent_source_id.description: A file a PC agent registered for clipmux push --local.

renditions.description: Replaces the asset's choice for this output and the ones after it; leave it out to keep it.

playback_id.description: The signed playback ID the link owns.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working, or null for never.

views_30d.description: Views over the last 30 UTC days, in lists.

body.description: Exactly what a webhook endpoint receives.

id.description: The event ID (evt_...), the same as X-Webhook-Id. Dedupe on it.

data.description: The asset when the event was made. Re-fetch it before acting.

job.description: The job behind the event, for re-encodes.

base_url.description: The media origin playback URLs start with.

max_token_lifetime_seconds.description: The longest a playback token may last: exp - iat.

upload_origins.description: Where a browser sends upload parts: this server (filesystem storage) and each bucket's public endpoint. With base_url, what a page with the uploader and player must allow in its Content-Security-Policy.

signing_keys.description: The keys that still verify tokens, newest first.

SharePlayback.description: Also the shape @clipmux/player's session-url expects from an app's own handler.

code.description: Show it; the owner checks it matches on verify_url. Any case, the dash optional.

api_key.description: A new API key with the default scopes. Shown once.

webhook_secret.description: Present when a webhook URL was given.

env.description: The same values as a .env block.

Renditions.description: The ladder rungs to encode, e.g. ["1080p", "480p"]. Rungs above the source are skipped; if none chosen fits, the largest rung that fits is encoded. Leave it out for every rung up to the source. Shown largest first.

apiKey.description: An app's API key (cmx_…), from your backend only. Scopes: uploads:write, assets:read, assets:write, analytics:read.

uploadToken.description: An upload's upload_token: safe for the browser, reaches only that upload.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A retry with the same key and request returns the first response; a different request is 422 idempotency_key_reused.

WebhookSignature.name: X-Webhook-Signature
WebhookSignature.description: sha256= and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of "{timestamp}.{raw body}", keyed with the endpoint secret (whsec_…, prefix included).

tags.name: Uploads
tags.description: Resumable browser uploads. Your backend creates the upload; the browser sends S3 multipart parts straight to storage with the upload token, then completes it.

tags.name: Videos
tags.description: A video is an asset in the API: its status, playback IDs, tracks and renditions. Find one by your own `passthrough`, page through changes, rename, re-encode or delete it.

tags.name: Subtitles and chapters
tags.description: Tracks made after a video is ready: subtitles from speech, and chapters from an LLM. A new track replaces the old one only once it is ready.

tags.name: Playback IDs
tags.description: Each video has one or more playback IDs, public or signed, each revocable on its own.

tags.name: Share links
tags.description: A share link plays one video for anyone holding its URL, until it expires or is revoked.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: The same events your webhook endpoints receive, read by long-polling. `npx @clipmux/node listen` uses it.

tags.name: App
tags.description: The API key's own app: its URLs, scopes, token lifetime and signing keys.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Views, watch time, unique viewers and bytes delivered, counted at delivery. Needs the `analytics:read` scope.

tags.name: App pairing
tags.description: How `npx @clipmux/node init` gets an app's credentials without anyone copying a secret. None of these routes needs a key.

tags.name: Share page
tags.description: The token endpoint behind a share link's page. It needs no session or key.

tags.name: Delivery
tags.description: Playback, from the media URL (`base_url`): HLS playlists, posters and subtitle files. Signed playback IDs take an ES256 token your backend signs; public ones take none.
